The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The test `testPcts()` in `FrequencyTest` is failing due to an incorrect implementation in the `Frequency` class concerning the `getPct(Object)` method. The bug report describes that `getPct(Object)` uses `getCumPct(Comparable)` instead of `getPct(Comparable)`. 

Inspecting the code shows the following:
- The `getPct(Object v)` method is marked as `@Deprecated` and returns `getCumPct((Comparable<?>) v)`. This means it returns the cumulative percentage rather than the simple percentage as intended.
- The `getCumPct(Comparable<?> v)` method calculates the cumulative frequency percentage correctly by dividing cumulative frequency by the sum of frequencies.
- The non-deprecated and proper `getPct(Comparable<?> v)` method returns the simple percentage by dividing the count of the given value by the sum of frequencies.

The test case `testPcts()` explicitly calls `f.getPct((Object)(Integer.valueOf(3)))` expecting the simple percentage (count of 3 divided by total), but because the deprecated `getPct(Object)` forwards to `getCumPct` instead of `getPct(Comparable)`, it returns the cumulative percentage instead. This results in failing assertions where the percentages are not matching expected values.

The root cause is the deprecated method `getPct(Object)` incorrectly delegating to `getCumPct(Comparable)` rather than forwarding to the non-deprecated and correct `getPct(Comparable)` method.

This fix is critical especially because the deprecated method is still in use in test cases and possibly client code, causing behavior changes between versions.

Suggested fix: Update `getPct(Object)` so that it calls `getPct(Comparable)` internally rather than `getCumPct(Comparable)`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
